chapter: Europe 1933, New York Cotton Club, Hodges group
title: Slippery Horn and other dates on the England trip
summary: Brown had never heard that Slippery Horn was named for him and recalls two theaters and many private parties.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Tate's. Are you -- no, I guess it was Stanley Dance says that Duke says he named "Slippery Horn" because the title was inspired by your playing. Did he tell you that?
No. I never heard that. "Slippery Horn" uh-huh.
I didn't realize that. I made so many numbers I really don't have any recollection of the times.
And that trip to Europe you played England, and you played for members of the royal family. Where else did you go?

We played two theaters, which the names have slipped me. And as I say again, so many -- we played so many private parties and things that the bookkeeping got all mixed up as to how many we really had played. But they did very well on that trip.
